stories.title: Canada proposes ban on fees for moving investment accounts
stories.summary: The federal government has released draft regulations to stop banks from charging fees when a client moves an investment account to another financial institution. The change would cover registered accounts such as RRSPs, TFSAs and RESPs, as well as non‑registered investment accounts held at Canadian banks. A regulatory impact analysis notes the fees are typically about $150 per account.
stories.why: It would reduce costs for Canadians who switch providers, potentially increasing competition in the banking sector.

stories.title: US stocks tumble as AI regulation fears trigger steep Nasdaq drop
stories.summary: The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.46% (down 1,421.5 points to 24,315.02), its biggest one‑day decline in 19 months, while the S&P 500 lost 4.32% (down 331.94 points to 7,353.65) and the Dow Jones slipped 3.45% (down 1,842.69 points to 51,513.43). The sell‑off was driven by concerns that tighter AI regulation from a Democrat‑controlled Congress could curb chipmaker and data‑centre investment, and by Fed officials’ comments on possible further rate hikes.
stories.why: The decline raises risk concerns for AI‑related and broader equities, influencing global investors and Indian market sentiment.

stories.title: OpenAI released a new cybersecurity model. Is that enough?
stories.summary: Max Justicz, the chief technology officer and co-founder of the startup Charge Robotics, used an OpenAI model to find a severe vulnerability that — if exploited — could allow hackers to take control of servers running Ubuntu, a widely used open source Linux-based operating system. Justicz, who has a hobbyist’s interest in cybersecurity and previously found a vulnerability in the same codebase, told TechCrunch that he found this issue using GPT 5.6 Sol, released in July, through the AI maker’s Daybreak Blue, a program that gives cybersecurity defenders access to powerful frontier models.
stories.why: This matters because it could change AI capabilities, costs, adoption, regulation or competitive positioning.

stories.title: US midterm victory unlikely to affect India‑US interim trade deal
stories.summary: Sources said the Democrats’ sweeping win in the U.S. midterm elections is not expected to impact the India‑U.S. interim trade agreement because the pact does not require formal Congressional ratification. The deal could still face challenges from ongoing U.S. Section 301 investigations into forced‑labour practices and excess industrial capacity that may affect tariff policy and finalisation.
stories.why: Trade developments can affect currencies, business costs, market access and the external balance of the economies involved.
